33.steps:
1. Configure L2 bridged mode between X0 and X2 (LAN and DMZ).
  2. On a PC on the LAN, set the default gateway to be the firewalls LAN IP address (192.168.168.168).
  3. Send traffic from the LAN PC to the internet.
  4. Verify that the default route is used to send packets out through the WAN.
33.title: Traffic is forwarded through the default gateway configured on the firewall, if the PC on the LAN has the default gateway as the firewalls IP.
33.result: Verify that the firewalls default route is used to send packets out through the WAN.

32.steps:
1. Bridge the LAN and DMZ.
  2. Add a 121 NAT policy between the WAN and the LAN.
  3. Under Firewall -> Access Rules, click on WAN-LAN and add an access policy which allows ICMP traffic from the WAN to the LAN.
  4. Initiate a ping from the WAN PC to the LAN PC.
  5. Verify success.
  6. Verify traffic from LAN to WAN is allowed (by default)
  7. Change the access rule to deny from LAN to WAN
  8. Verify traffic from LAN to WAN get blocked
32.title: Access rules for WAN-LAN (Mixed mode)

63.steps:
1. Configure LAN-DMZ in bridged mode.
  2. Configure a 121 NAT between the WAN and the LAN.
  3. Access a Telnet client on the WAN and telnet to the LAN PC.
  4. Verify that the telnet session should be successful.
63.initial: A telnet server on the LAN.
63.title: Telnet
63.result: Verify that the Telnet session should be successful when LAN-DMZ/WAN-LAN are in bridged mode

21.steps:
1) Configure an interface eg X1 as WAN (Primary bridged Interface)
  2) Configure interface X2 as LAN, bridging it to the X1 interface. (Secondary bridged interface).
  3) Go to Network -> Routing and try to configure OSPF on X1 or X2.
  4) Verify that OSPF cannot be enabled on X1 or X2.
21.title: Verify that OSPF cannot be configured on any of the bridged interfaces
21.result: OSPF cannot be configured on any of the bridged interfaces.

71.title: L2 Bridge with CLI
71.result: There should be no error coming up in cli.

7.steps:

  2) Configure interface X2 as LAN and try bridging it to interface X1.
  3) Verify that an error message appears.
7.title: Verify that only static addressing should be used for the Primary Bridged interface
7.result: Only static addressing should be used for the Primary Bridge interface.

26.steps:

  2. Bridge the WLAN to the LAN/DMZ.
  3. Connect from a wireless client to the wireless network specified by the SSID of the SonicPoint.
  4. Access the servers/PCs on LAN/DMZ.
  5. Verify success.

26.result: The wireless client can access the servers/PCs on LAN/DMZ successfully.

18.steps:
1) Configure an interface eg X1 as WAN (Primary bridged Interface).
  2) Configure interface X2 as LAN, bridging it to the X1 interface. (Secondary bridged interface).
  3) Go to Network -> Interfaces and click on X1 and X2.
  4) Verify that the checkbox Enable Multicast should be grayed out for interfaces X1 and X2.
  5) Configure X2 as a normal interface as LAN.
  6) Repeat steps 3 and 4.
  7) Verify that the checkbox should not be grayed out for X1 and X2.

18.result: IGMP is not supported on bridged interfaces.

72.title: Traffic coming from a VLAN on a bridged interface can be forwarded to the correct vlan sub-interface by FW

16.steps:
1) Configure an interface eg X1 as WAN (Primary bridged Interface).
  2) Configure interface X2 as LAN, bridging it to the X1 interface. (Secondary bridged interface).
  3) Go to Network -> DHCP server and configure a dynamic range. On Dynamic Range Configuration window, X2 should not be listed in the interface drop-down list.
  4) Configure X2 as a normal interface as LAN.
  5) Repeat steps 3.
  6) Verify that X2 is shown in the interface drop-down list and DHCP range can be created.
  7) Bridge X3 to X0 without disabling X0 DHCP range.
  8) You should get error message: DHCP Server enabled on primary bridged interface - not supported.

16.result: As mentioned in above steps, DHCP server is not supported on bridged interfaces.

44.result: The LAN and the WAN are normal interfaces with static IP addresses after the box restarts.

55.steps:

  3. On the virus server, try to access/download a Virus.
  4. Verify that the first time, a prompt for downloading the virus. The second time, an error page is displayed, stating that GAV blocks the virus.
  5. Verify that a log message comes up, under Log stating that GAV blocks the virus.

  5. Verify that a log message comes up, under Log stating that AV blocks the spyware file.

10.steps:
1) Configure a VPN tunnel between the LAN of the local firewall (one of the bridged interfaces) and the LAN of the remote firewall.

  3) Verify from the VPN page that the tunnel is up.

A bridged interface LAN-LAN or LAN-DMZ on the local firewall
  See DTS:51789
  For Gen5 a route must be added since it is abiguous which addresses may be on the WAN and which may be on the LAN:
  Source: ANY Dest: <custom address object of addresses on the LAN &gt:
  Service: ANY Gateway: 0.0.0.0 Interface: X0

31.steps:

  2. Connect PC2 to X1, gateway X1's IP, connect PC2 to X3, gateway X3's IP.
  3. By default, traffic is denied from WAN to DMZ, but allowed from DMZ to WAN.
  4. Ping PC2 from PC3 to verify traffic from DMZ to WAN is allowed, ping PC3 from PC2 to verify traffic from WAN to DMZ is blocked.
  5. Change the access rule to allow from WAN to DMZ, but deny from DMZ to WAN.
  6. Ping PC2 from PC3 to verify traffic from DMZ to WAN is blocked, ping PC3 from PC2 to verify traffic from WAN to DMZ is allowed.

77.steps:

  3. Pass traffic from the LAN PC to the WAN PC.
  3. Initiate failover.
  4. Verify that the Backup firewall becomes Active and that the traffic is still passing through.
  5. Do Failback.
  6. Verify that the Primary firewall becomes Active and that the traffic is still passing through.

64.result: Failover and Failback should work as defined, when WAN-LAN are configured in Bridged mode.

58.steps:
1. Configure WAN-LAN in bridged mode.
  2. Make sure firewall is licensed for CFS. Enable CFS on WAN and LAN zone.
  3. Go to page Security Services > Content Filter. In the drop-down list of CFS Policy Assignment, select Via App Rules.
  4. Create a match object: cfs_ob1 - CFS Category List - 30: E-Mail & 38: Shopping.
  5. Create an action object: cfs_act_ob1 - HTTP Block Page - You are not allowed to visit the website.
  6. Add an App Rule: cfs_policy1 -- CFS -- cfs_ob1 -- cfs_act_ob1.
  7. From a LAN PC, try to visit www.hotmail.com, www.amazon.com and www.google.com.
58.title: CFS
58.result: Traffic to hotmail and amazon will be blocked by cfs-poli-1, Traffic to google will be successed.

28.title: Access rules for WAN-DMZ (Pure L2 mode)

75.steps:
1. Set interface X2 as WAN static, bridge LAN interface X3 to X2, set interface X4 as LAN static.
  2. Add a PBR with source: any, destination: 8.8.8.8, gateway: X4 Default Gateway, interface: X4, metric: 10.
  3. Keep capturing packets on PC2 and PC3.
  3. On PC1, set its gateway as X2's IP, then send continuous ping to 8.8.8.8. Verify packets captured on PC2 and PC3.
  5. Open X3's edit page, check the checkbox for option "Never route traffic on this bridge-pair" , click OK. Verify packets captured on PC2 and PC3 again.
75.title: Test the function for option "Never route traffic on this bridge-pair"
75.result:
Ping packets from PC1 to 8.8.8.8 can only be captured on PC3 when the option "Never route traffic on this bridge-pair" is not enabled.
  Ping packets from PC1 to 8.8.8.8 can only be captured on PC2 when the option "Never route traffic on this bridge-pair" is enabled.

40.steps:
1. Configure LAN-WAN in bridged mode.
  2. On a LAN side PC, set its gateway to be the bridged pair's IP, setup GVC configuration to connect to the remote office.
  3. Send some packets from the PC, then captue the packets received on remote office.
40.title: GVC from LAN to a remote office and checking if ESP packets are intact
40.result: The packets sent and received on both side are exactly the same.

14.steps:
1) Configure an interface eg X1 as WAN (Primary bridged Interface).
  2) Enable Wan Failover
  2) Configure interface X2 as LAN, bridging it to the X1 interface. (Secondary bridged interface)
  3) Verify that an error message should show up.
14.title: Verify that a bridged pair cannot be configured if Wan Failover and Load balancing is enabled
14.result: When Wan Failover and Load balancing is configured, bridged pair cannot be configured.

69.title: LAN bridged to default WAN doesn't affect other interfaces traffic
69.result: After congfig a lan->wan bridge pair(default WAN interface),other interfaces traffic is still forwarded as before.

59.steps:
Case1: Put the LAN and WAN interfaces as L2 bridge mode, no VLAN interfaces are created.
  Send VLAN tagged traffic from the Hosts connected to the LAN and WAN interfaces. ( Same VLAN is used from both the hosts )
  Case2:
  Create VLAN subinterfaces for LAN and WAN with different VLAN IDs and different static IP subnets.
  Send traffic from hosts connected to LAN and WAN with these different VLAN IDs.
59.initial:
Create a LAN and WAN interfaces and put them in L2 bridge mode with static IP.
  Either use Ixload with perr-peer traffic or just simple ICMP with LAN and WAN hosts to verify the data path.
59.title: Bump in the VLAN
59.result: In both case 1 and case2 bi-directional traffic should suceed.

49.steps:
1. Configure the WAN-LAN as a bridged pair.
  2. Under System -> Diagnostics, click the button Download TSR.
  3. You will be prompted to save the TSR.
  4. Open the TSR before/after saving it. Verify that the interfaces WAN and LAN are shown as bridged.
  5. Repeat the above testcases for LAN-DMZ bridged.
49.title: Download the TSR
49.result: The TSR should show that the interfaces WAN-LAN/LAN-DMZ as bridged to each other.

24.steps:
1. Configure interface X2 as WAN static(Primary bridged Interface).
  2. Configure interface X3 as LAN, bridging to interface X2. (Secondary bridged interface).
  3. On X3's edit page, VLAN Filtering tab, set filtering mode to Block listed VLANs, then move VLAN 100 to the right box which containing the listed VLANs.
  4. Send two tagged traffics from Ixia port1(e.x. ping Ixia port2's IP), one tagged with 100 and the other tagged with 200. Try to capture the packets on Ixia port2.
24.title: Access rules denying traffic to/from a particular VLAN
24.result: Traffic tagged with 100 failed, and traffic tagged with 200 succeed.

53.steps:
1. Configure LAN-DMZ in bridged mode.
  2. Configure GMS settings under System -> Administration and choose the GMS management using existing tunnel.
  3. Login the GMS server, connect to firewall using existing tunnel.
  4. Manage the firewall using the GMS server. Make some configuration changes, verify if the interfaces can be unconfigured from bridged mode and can be reconfigured as bridged mode.
53.title: GMS management using existing tunnel
53.result: GMS management of the firewall is possible and interfaces can be configured in and out of bridged mode from the GMS server.

22.steps:
1. Create a subinterface for X1 with VLAN ID 100.
  2. Create a subinterface for X2 with VLAN ID 100.
  3. Verify success.
22.title: Verify that primary and secondary interfaces can have sub-interfaces configured with same VLAN ID
22.result: Primary and secondary interfaces can have subinterfaces configured with same VLAN ID.

42.steps:
1. Reboot the firewall from factory defaults.
  2. Configure the LAN, WAN and DMZ.
  3. Bridge the LAN and the DMZ.
  4. Click on Register the unit under System -> Status page.
  5. Enter the username and password.
  6. Verify that the box can be registered.
42.title: Verify that the box can be registered when X1 is not the Primary bridge interface.

46.steps:
1. Configure a bridged pair between the WAN and the LAN.
  2. Export prefs.
  3. Configure the WAN with DHCP/PPPoE.
  4. Import prefs.
  5. Verify that after the box restarts, the LAN and WAN should be bridged. The WAN should not have Dynamic addressing.
46.title: Bridged pair export prefs, WAN IP to Dynamic Addressing, import prefs.
46.result: The WAN and the LAN are bridged after the box restarts.

23.steps:
1. Configure interface X2 as LAN static, bridge LAN interface X3 to X2.
  2. Connect a PC to X2 as the DHCP client, start a DHCP server on the side of X3.
  3. Set the PC's NIC's mode as Obtain an IP address automatically, try to get a DHCP lease from the server.
23.title: Verify that DHCP can be passed through the bridged interfaces
23.result: The PC on X2 can obtain DHCP lease from DHCP server on X3 successfully.

13.steps:
1. Configure a bridged pair between LAN and DMZ.
  2. Connect two Ixia ports to both of the pair interfaces.
  3. Check the checkbox Block NonIPV4 traffic on the secondary bridged interface.
  4. Send IPX traffic from the Ixia port on LAN to DMZ.
  5. Verify if the Ixia port on DMZ receives the IPX packets.
  6. Repeat steps 4 and 5 with other types of nonIPv4 traffics, such as STP BPDU, LADP, PPPOE Discovery, LLTD, LLDP, CDP, QinQ, PAgP and so on.
13.title: Non IPV4 traffic is blocked by the Bridged pair
13.result: NonIPV4 traffic is blocked by the bridged pair.

6.steps:
1) Configure an interface eg X1 as WAN (Primary bridged Interface)
  2) Configure interface X2 as LAN
  3) Add a sub-interface to X2.
  4) Try bridging the sub-interface configured above to X1.
  5) Verify that an error message appears.
6.title: Verify that a sub-interface cannot be configured as a bridged pair.
6.result: A sub-interface cannot be configured as a bridge interface.

36.steps:
1. Set interface X1 as WAN static, bridge X0 to X1.
  2. Connect a PC to X0, set its NIC to obtain an IP addresss automatically; connect X1 to the Internet.
  3. Try to access the Internet on the PC.
  4. On Firewall->Access Rules page, change LAN->WAN default ACL's "Users Included" from ALL to Administrator, try to access the Internet on the PC again.
  5. Login FW using administrator account from X0 on the PC, then try to access the Internet once more.
  6. Try the controllability of ULA for other users such as Guests, Trusted Users and so on.
36.title: ULA
36.result:
In step 3, the Internet can be accessed.
  In step 4, the Internet can't be accessed.
  In step 5, the Internet can be accessed.

3.steps:
1) Configure an interface eg X1 as WAN (Primary bridged Interface)
  2) Configure interface X2 as LAN, bridging it to the X1 interface. (Secondary bridged interface).
  3) Verify that the Network -> Interfaces page displays X1 and X2 sharing the same IP. 4) Configure X3 as LAN.
  5) Configure X4 as WAN. When trying to bridge it to X3 interface, verify that there is no such option available for the WAN interface.
3.title: Verifying that the WAN cannot be configured as the secondary interface
3.result: No option for bridging the WAN interface to any other interface should be available.

9.steps:
1. Initiate an FTP session between 2 PCs.
  2. Configure LAN-DMZ as a bridged pair.
  3. Connect the 2 PCs into the respective LAN and DMZ hubs.
  4. Initiate an FTP session again.
  5. Verify that the FTP session is successful.
9.title: Stream based connections
9.result: The FTP session should be successfully established between the 2 PCs.

51.steps:
1. Configure LAN-DMZ in bridged mode.
  2. Configure GMS settings under System -> Administration and choose the GMS management using IPSec tunnel.
  3. Login the GMS server, connect to firewall using Ipsec tunnel.
  4. Manage the firewall using the GMS server. Make some configuration changes, verify if the interfaces can be unconfigured from bridged mode and can be reconfigured as bridged mode.
  Enable the GMS admin using IPsec Management Tunnel
  Copy the Encryption Key and Authentication Key so that they can be entered into the GMS GUI.
  On the GMS GUI , click add unit.
  Specify the serial number of the firewall to be managed, sepcify the managed address manually( wan ip )
  management mode = using management tunnel
  paste the encryption key and authentcation kjey here obtained from the DUT.
  After the node is synced( i.e. turns blue) check the system -> status -> management -> Management Mode : Should show as "Management Tunnel "
51.initial:
GMS server present, which is able to communicate to the firewall. It should be configured for IPSec management
  In order to configure GMS server for IPsec management, GMS server agent needs to be connected to a GMS gateway ( i.e. any sonicwall firewall) .
  Specify the gateway information ( Firewall IP and login info ) under the following on GMS server:
  In the GMS admin GUI -> Console -> Management -> Agents -> gateway configuration.
  Give the firewall IP that is serving as the gateway.
51.title: GMS management using IPSec tunnel
51.result: GMS management of the firewall is possible and interfaces can be configured in and out of bridged mode from the GMS server.

47.steps:
1. Configure WAN and LAN in bridged mode.
  2. Send traffic from the LAN to the WAN.
  3. Verify success.
  4. Reboot the box.
  5. After the box comes back up, verify that traffic can be successfully sent from the LAN to the WAN.
47.title: Bridged pair  Reboot box.
47.result: The traffic can be successfully sent from the LAN to the WAN.

8.steps:
1) Configure an interface eg X1 as WAN (Primary bridged Interface)
  2) Configure interface X2 as LAN, bridging it to the X1 interface. (Secondary bridged interface)
  3) Verify that the Network -> Interfaces page displays X1 and X2 sharing the same IP.
  4) Change the IP address of X1.
  5) Verify that the Network -> Interfaces page displays X1 and X2 sharing the same IP(the new IP address configured in Step 4).
8.title: Verify that changing the IP address of the Primary bridge interface should also be reflected in the Secondary bridge interface
8.result: Changing the IP address of the Primary bridge interface should be reflected in the Secondary bridge interface.

38.initial: 2 WANs present. (Do I need to test it with WAN - LAN bridged pair. If it is WAN-LAN bridged pair, then the LAN PC will have the default gateway as X1s default gateway. So would it actually work?)
38.title: Bridged pair does not interfere with PBR.
38.result:
The Policy based routes are not affected when LAN and DMZ are configured as bridged pair.
  According to the PBR,the traffic should be forwarded to the correct interface
  of the DUT

4.steps:
1. Bridge DMZ interface X2 to LAN static interface X0.
  2. Bridge LAN interface X3 to WAN static interface X1.
  3. Bridge other interfaces in different zones as many as possible, check the status of the FW and the function of the pairs.
4.title: Verifying Maximum number of pairings for a specific platform Eg NSA6600
4.result: The number of Bridged interface is not limited, make sure no exception occurs when there are a number of bridged interfaces configured.

34.steps:
1. Configure L2 bridged mode between X0 and X2 (LAN and DMZ).
  2. On a PC on the LAN, set the default gateway to be a bogus IP address (1.1.1.1).
  3. Configure a static arp entry on the LAN PC (arp -s 1.1.1.1 00-b0-d0-e6-d0-65) where the MAC address is the PC on the DMZ side. 3. Send traffic from the LAN PC to the internet.
  4. Verify that the firewall acts as a bridge than a router and the packets travel through the other bridged interface.
34.title: Traffic gets forwarded to the bridged other interface, when the PC on the LAN has the default gateway configured on it as a bogus IP address
34.result: Verify that the traffic gets forwarded to the other bridged interface, if the LAN PC has a bogus IP configured as its default gateway.

37.steps:
1. Configure L2 bridged mode between X0 and X2 (LAN and DMZ).
  2. On a PC on the LAN, set the default gateway to be the X0's IP address.
  3. On DMZ side, setup a LDAP server. On FW, set User authentication method to be LDAP on Users->Settings page and create a new user.
  4. Log into firewall from the LAN using the new created user.
  5. Access the WAN.
37.title: LDAP
37.result: The user can login FW successfully and WAN can be accessed through the bridge from the LAN PC.

43.steps:
1. Configure a bridged pair between the WAN and the LAN.
  2. Export prefs.
  3. Configure the LAN and WAN as normal interfaces with static addresses.
  4. Import prefs.
  5. Verify that after the box restarts, the WAN and LAN should be bridged.
43.title: Bridged pair export prefs, Normal interfaces, import prefs
43.result: The WAN and the LAN are bridged after the box restarts.

5.steps:
1) Configure an interface eg X1 as WAN with IP 1.1.1.1 (Primary bridged interface)
  2) Configure X2 as LAN and bridge it to X1 (Secondary bridged interface).
  3) Configure interface X3 as DMZ and try giving it the IP 1.1.1.1
  4) Verify that an error is got.
5.title: Verify that any other interface on the firewall cannot have the same IP as that of the bridged pair
5.result: Any other interface on the firewall cannot have the same IP as that of the bridged pair.
